answers.text: Sending the longest, most detailed first reply possible

answers.text: Speed of response — a prompt acknowledgment within an hour beats a polished reply hours later

questions.feedback: Inquiries cool quickly. A short, prompt acknowledgment converts dramatically better than a perfect reply that arrives hours later.
questions.feedbackHtml: Speed of response is the highest-leverage variable in lead conversion.

questions.question: What rough talking ratio should hold during a discovery conversation?
questions.questionHtml: What rough talking ratio should hold during a discovery conversation?

answers.text: You speak 70%, the customer speaks 30%
answers.textHtml: You speak 70%, the customer speaks 30%

answers.text: Roughly equal — 50/50
answers.textHtml: Roughly equal — 50/50

answers.text: The customer should talk roughly twice as much as you
answers.textHtml: The customer should talk roughly twice as much as you

answers.text: You speak only at the end with the price
answers.textHtml: You speak only at the end with the price

questions.feedback: Aim for the customer to talk twice as much as you. If you are doing more than 40% of the talking, switch to listening mode — questions build trust faster than pitching.
questions.feedbackHtml: Customer talks roughly two-thirds of the time; you ask and listen.

answers.textHtml: It signals desperation and forces a discount

questions.feedback: Three-tier proposals raise average deal size, reduce sticker shock, and let customers anchor on a 'middle' option. They do not signal desperation when tiers genuinely differ in deliverables.

questions.question: What should you do immediately after stating a price out loud?
questions.questionHtml: What should you do immediately after stating a price out loud?

answers.text: Quickly add 'but I might be able to discount it'
answers.textHtml: Quickly add 'but I might be able to discount it'

answers.text: Stay silent for at least three seconds and let the customer respond first
answers.textHtml: Stay silent for at least three seconds and let the customer respond first

answers.text: Repeat the price louder
answers.textHtml: Repeat the price louder

answers.text: Apologise for it being high
answers.textHtml: Apologise for it being high

questions.feedback: Stay silent. The first person to speak after a price is named tends to give ground. Pre-discounting before the customer even reacts trains them to expect it next time.
questions.feedbackHtml: Say the price calmly, stay silent for several seconds, never pre-discount.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle the objection 'It's too expensive'?
questions.questionHtml: What is the best way to handle the objection 'It's too expensive'?

answers.text: Immediately offer a discount
answers.textHtml: Immediately offer a discount

answers.text: Defend your rate by listing your equipment and certifications
answers.textHtml: Defend your rate by listing your equipment and certifications

answers.text: Acknowledge, ask a clarifying question (e.g. 'compared to what?'), then reframe — usually adjusting scope rather than rate
answers.textHtml: Acknowledge, ask a clarifying question (e.g. 'compared to what?'), then reframe — usually adjusting scope rather than rate

answers.text: Send a more polished proposal
answers.textHtml: Send a more polished proposal

questions.feedback: Acknowledge, ask, reframe. 'Too expensive' often means 'I don't yet see the value' or 'the scope is heavier than I need.' Asking 'compared to what?' separates those situations and keeps the rate intact.
questions.feedbackHtml: Use the acknowledge-ask-reframe pattern; adjust scope, not rate.
